caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing after applying six different editing methods to the BioMedLM model, with accuracy measured across varying co-occurrence numbers on a logarithmic scale. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," spans from 0 to 10^3 on a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 40% to 65% on a linear scale, with tick marks every 5 percentage points. Six distinct lines represent different methods: Base (black circles, solid line), MEND (brown diamonds, solid line), FT (blue triangles, solid line), MEMIT (purple squares, solid line), IKE (red triangles, solid line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). All lines show an increasing trend in accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers. ROME starts at approximately 51% at the lowest co-occurrence number and rises to about 66% at 10^3. MEND begins near 44% and reaches approximately 56% at 10^3, while MEMIT starts at about 44% and ends near 55%. IKE starts at approximately 43% and increases to around 52% at 10^3, surpassing FT (which starts at about 40% and ends near 48%) after co-occurrence numbers exceed 10^2. The Base model begins at approximately 39% and plateaus at about 44% across the range.
